# dlatsqr

> Computes a blocked Tall-Skinny QR (TSQR) factorization of a real `M`-by-`N` matrix (with `M >= N`).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlatsqr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlatsqr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlatsqr( order, M, N, mb, nb, A, LDA, T, LDT, WORK ) → integer
```

Computes a blocked Tall-Skinny QR (TSQR) factorization of a real `M`-by-`N` matrix `A` (with `M >= N`).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of the matrix `A` (`M >= N`)<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of the matrix `A`<br>Rejects `N < 0 \|\| M < N` |
| `mb` | `integer` | Row block size (`mb >= 1`)<br>Rejects `mb < 1` |
| `nb` | `integer` | Column block size (`1 <= nb <= N` when `N > 0`)<br>Rejects `nb < 1 \|\| (nb > N && N > 0)` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Column-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, M)`<br>Row-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nb × N*NUMBER_OF_ROW_BLOCKS</sub> | **out** · Output matrix of upper triangular block reflector factors |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `T`<br>Requires `LDT ≥ nb` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N * nb</sub> | **out** · Workspace array of length at least `nb*N` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $M \ge N \ge 0$.
- `mb`: The row block size to be used in the blocked QR. $\mathrm{MB} > 0$.
- `nb`: The column block size to be used in the blocked QR. $N \ge \mathrm{NB} \ge 1$.
- `A`: On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, the elements on and above the diagonal of the array contain the N-by-N upper triangular matrix R; the elements below the diagonal represent Q by the columns of blocked V (see Further Details).
- `T`: dimension (`LDT`, N \* Number\_of\_row\_blocks) where Number\_of\_row\_blocks = CEIL((M-N)/(`MB`-N)) The blocked upper triangular block reflectors stored in compact form as a sequence of upper triangular blocks. See Further Details below.
- `WORK`: ```text
  (workspace) DOUBLE PRECISION array, dimension (MAX(1,LWORK))
  ```

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `N < 0 \|\| M < N`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `mb < 1`)
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `nb < 1 \|\| ( nb > N && N > 0 )`)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `nb` (column-major)
- `RangeError` `LDA` must be valid for the chosen order

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlatsqr.strided(
    M, N,
    mb, nb,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Computes a blocked Tall-Skinny QR (TSQR) factorization of a real `M`-by-`N` matrix `A` (with `M >= N`).

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of the matrix `A` (`M >= N`)<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of the matrix `A`<br>Rejects `N < 0 \|\| M < N` |
| `mb` | `integer` | Row block size (`mb >= 1`)<br>Rejects `mb < 1` |
| `nb` | `integer` | Column block size (`1 <= nb <= N` when `N > 0`)<br>Rejects `nb < 1 \|\| (nb > N && N > 0)` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nb × N*NUMBER_OF_ROW_BLOCKS</sub> | **out** · Output matrix of upper triangular block reflector factors |
| ↳ `strideT1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `T` |
| ↳ `strideT2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `T` |
| ↳ `offsetT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `T` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N * nb</sub> | **out** · Workspace array of length at least `nb*N` |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $M \ge N \ge 0$.
- `mb`: The row block size to be used in the blocked QR. $\mathrm{MB} > 0$.
- `nb`: The column block size to be used in the blocked QR. $N \ge \mathrm{NB} \ge 1$.
- `A`: On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, the elements on and above the diagonal of the array contain the N-by-N upper triangular matrix R; the elements below the diagonal represent Q by the columns of blocked V (see Further Details).
- `T`: dimension (`LDT`, N \* Number\_of\_row\_blocks) where Number\_of\_row\_blocks = CEIL((M-N)/(`MB`-N)) The blocked upper triangular block reflectors stored in compact form as a sequence of upper triangular blocks. See Further Details below.
- `WORK`: ```text
  (workspace) DOUBLE PRECISION array, dimension (MAX(1,LWORK))
  ```

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `N < 0 \|\| M < N`)
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `mb < 1`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `nb < 1 \|\| ( nb > N && N > 0 )`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `min( M, N ) === 0` or `mb <= N || mb >= M`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlatsqr()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLATSQR`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlatsqr.f).
-   The factorization is appropriate for tall-skinny matrices where `M >> N`. The first row block of size `mb`-by-`N` is factored via `dgeqrt`; subsequent row blocks are combined into the running `R` factor via `dtpqrt`.
-   `T` has dimensions `nb`-by-`(N * Number_of_row_blocks)` where `Number_of_row_blocks = ceil((M-N)/(mb-N))`. When `mb <= N` or `mb >= M`, the routine simply calls `dgeqrt` and `T` is `nb`-by-`N`.
-   The orthogonal factor `Q` is represented implicitly by the Householder reflectors stored below the diagonal of `A` together with `T`; use `dgemqrt` (or a future `dlamtsqr`) to apply `Q` or `Q^T`.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlatsqr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlatsqr';

// 8-by-3 column-major matrix:
const M = 8;
const N = 3;
const mb = 4;
const nb = 2;
const A = new Float64Array([
	5.0,
	0.5,
	0.333,
	0.25,
	0.2,
	0.167,
	0.143,
	0.125,
	0.5,
	6.0,
	0.5,
	0.333,
	0.25,
	0.2,
	0.167,
	0.143,
	0.333,
	0.5,
	7.0,
	0.5,
	0.333,
	0.25,
	0.2,
	0.167
]);

// T storage: nb-by-(N * Number_of_row_blocks); Number_of_row_blocks = ceil((M-N)/(mb-N)) = 5.
const T = new Float64Array( nb * N * 5 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( nb * N );

const info = dlatsqr( 'column-major', M, N, mb, nb, A, M, T, nb, WORK );
console.log( 'info = %d', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( A ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLATSQR`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLATSQR computes a blocked Tall-Skinny QR factorization of a real M-by-N matrix A for $M \ge N$:

$$
A = Q \, \begin{pmatrix} R \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}
$$

where:

Q is a M-by-M orthogonal matrix, stored on exit in an implicit form in the elements below the diagonal of the array A and in the elements of the array T;

R is an upper-triangular N-by-N matrix, stored on exit in the elements on and above the diagonal of the array A.

0 is a (M-N)-by-N zero matrix, and is not stored.

### Further Details

Tall-Skinny QR (TSQR) performs QR by a sequence of orthogonal transformations, representing Q as a product of other orthogonal matrices

$$
Q = Q(1) \, Q(2) \, \cdots \, Q(k)
$$

where each Q(i) zeros out subdiagonal entries of a block of `MB` rows of A:

-   Q(1) zeros out the subdiagonal entries of rows 1:`MB` of A
-   Q(2) zeros out the bottom `MB`-N rows of rows \[1:N,`MB`+1:$2 \, \mathrm{MB}-N$\] of A
-   Q(3) zeros out the bottom `MB`-N rows of rows \[1:N,$2 \, \mathrm{MB}-N+1$:$3 \, \mathrm{MB}-2 \, N$\] of A
-   . . .

Q(1) is computed by GEQRT, which represents Q(1) by Householder vectors stored under the diagonal of rows 1:`MB` of A, and by upper triangular block reflectors, stored in array `T(1:LDT,1:N)`. For more information see Further Details in GEQRT.

Q(i) for $i>1$ is computed by TPQRT, which represents Q(i) by Householder vectors stored in rows \[$(i-1) \, (\mathrm{MB}-N)+N+1$:$i \, (\mathrm{MB}-N)+N$\] of A, and by upper triangular block reflectors, stored in array `T(1:LDT,(i-1)*N+1:i*N)`. The last Q(k) may use fewer rows. For more information see Further Details in TPQRT.

For more details of the overall algorithm, see the description of Sequential TSQR in Section 2.2 of \[1\].

\[1\] “Communication-Optimal Parallel and Sequential QR and LU Factorizations,”

-   J. Demmel, L. Grigori, M. Hoemmen, J. Langou,
-   SIAM J. Sci. Comput, vol. 34, no. 1, 2012

</section>
